## Layering Access: From Recipe to Shelf {#three-levels .slide-dark background-color="#1A1D20" transition="fade" transition-speed="fast" background-transition="fade"}

::: {.lede}
Each layer trades flexibility for expanded access.
:::

::: {.notes}
*⏱ 1:15 · Jadey, one Tanya interjection*

**Jadey:** Well, we have a similar evolution story around expanding access. But instead of cookies, we made it easier for cooperators to generate soil health reports for farmers to better understand their data.  

**[click: Layer 1, the center figure]** At the center is the recipe that lives in on a notepad in your kitchen. Only you have access to it. That's the template. **[click: Layer 2, ring 2]** But if you want other bakers to use it, you need to publish the recipe in a cookbook. In our case, we created an R package to allow experienced coders to reuse and adapt the recipe. **[click: Layer 3, ring 3]** The shelf is different. You don't need to know the recipe or even how to bake. With our Shiny app, you can make soil health reports without the template or knowing R.

In our story, I'm Ruth. I made the recipe and published it in a cookbook.

**Tanya:** And if she's Ruth, I guess that makes me Nestlé. Together, we brought Jadey's reports to the shelf with a Shiny app.

**Jadey:** Our main takeaway is that there's no single tool for everyone. Build the layer that meets the user where they are. So let's start at the beginning.
:::
